mission: CAIP was a non-partisan advocacy group that lobbied the US Congress from June 2023 to May 2025 for 'commonsense' laws against catastrophic AI risk. It drafted model legislation, endorsed bills, ran briefings and a podcast, and connected policymakers with experts before shutting down for lack of funding.

key_work.title: Model legislation for advanced AI
key_work.plain_summary: CAIP drafted a model bill for regulating advanced AI (licensing and oversight of the most powerful systems) and promoted it in Congress.

key_work.title: Whistleblower Protections for AI Employees
key_work.plain_summary: Shows how legal protections can let AI-company staff report dangers to authorities without breaching trade secrets.

key_work.title: AI Agents: Governing Autonomy in the Digital Age
key_work.plain_summary: A report on policies for increasingly autonomous AI agents that can act on their own online.

key_work.title: CAIP Has Shut Down (post-mortem)
key_work.plain_summary: A write-up explaining why CAIP closed: insufficient funding, some internal hiring mistakes, and what the authors see as funders' bias toward research over advocacy.

status_note: ran out of funding and ceased most operations around May–June 2025; keeps a volunteer legislative-review service and its Policy Advocacy Network; website preserved as an archive
status_raw: closed (mostly) — ran out of funding and ceased most operations around May–June 2025; keeps a volunteer legislative-review service and its Policy Advocacy Network; website preserved as an archive
funding_note: Initial funding from Lightspeed Grants and private donors (2023 announcement). Ceased most operations as of June 2025 for lack of funding; would need ~$150k/month to restart (CAIP donate page).
events: Center for AI Policy runs out of funding and ceases most operations

people.role: Co-founder and first CEO (left 2024; now AI Futures Project)

warnings.text: AI will be incredibly transformative and society is collectively unprepared for many of its worst risks.
Government lacks the capacity to quickly identify and respond to AI's national-security risks.
Increasingly autonomous AI agents create new risks that existing law does not cover.

recommendations.text: Pass federal legislation to oversee and license the most powerful AI systems.
Build government capacity to monitor and respond to AI risks.
